tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

2	name: windows-ui-testing-without-a-desktop
3	description: How to drive real JusPrin UI gestures on the Windows box when the RDP session is disconnected (SetCursorPos and screen capture both die; send WM_ messages and read geometry instead)
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: c818cfcf-07b0-4d84-a4d6-a69c1bd9fdde
8	  modified: 2026-10-22T01:22:43.199Z
9	---
10	
11	When the RDP session to the Windows verification box is **disconnected** (`query session` shows state `Disc` for the `guitest` session), `SetCursorPos`/`mouse_event` silently do nothing — `GetCursorPos` keeps returning 0,0 — and `Graphics.CopyFromScreen` throws "The handle is invalid". Only a *connected* session has an input desktop.
12	
13	**Why:** This looks exactly like an application bug — gestures appear to have no effect and screenshots fail — so it can burn a long time before you realise the session, not the code, is the problem.
14	
15	**How to apply:**
16	- Check `query session` first when input or capture stops working.
17	- Real UI testing still works without a desktop: `SendMessageTimeout` WM_LBUTTONDOWN / WM_MOUSEMOVE / WM_LBUTTONUP / WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK straight to the child HWND. This goes through the real wxMSW window procedure, real `SetCapture`, and real double-click handling — strictly more real than the harness's `ProcessEvent` injection, which bypasses `MSWWindowProc` entirely.
18	- A faithful drag must hold the pointer at a fixed **screen** x and recompute the client x from the target window's live `GetWindowRect` each step. Holding client x fixed makes a moving splitter run away, because the app converts with `ClientToScreen` against the window's current position.
19	- Screenshots still work disconnected through `PrintWindow(hwnd, hdc, 2)` (PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT): it draws the GL canvas and WebView2 panes (confirmed 2026-10-21). CopyFromScreen may not throw but returns a blank white image. But PrintWindow often returns the GL canvas as flat grey even at rest and after RedrawWindow (2026-10-22: grey in PrintWindow, tower drawn on screen). A grey canvas in a PrintWindow capture proves nothing; with a connected session, check with CopyFromScreen before calling it a bug or calling it fine.
20	- Read results from `EnumChildWindows` + `GetWindowRect` rather than pixels; assert that sibling columns tile the client rect exactly, which catches overlaps a per-window size check cannot see.
21	- P/Invoke `GetWindowTextW` must be declared `CharSet=CharSet.Unicode`, or the StringBuilder is marshalled as ANSI and the W call overruns the buffer and crashes PowerShell.
22	- The harness holds `shell_integration_harness.exe` open; kill it before relinking or the link fails with LNK1104.
23	- See [[windows-build-machine]] for the Mesa/GL and toolchain facts.
24

12	guard, then the user immediately found two things I never tried: the Agent chat panel
13	was still on screen, and clicking a project card led nowhere useful. Both were one
14	click away.

16	**Why:** I checked the *page* against the mockup instead of the *screen*, and I stopped
17	at "synthetic input is blocked on this machine" instead of finding another way in.
18	Worse, my capture method was `PrintWindow`, which renders OpenGL content black **and
19	omits modal dialogs entirely** — so my "verification" screenshots were structurally

24	- Before trusting a screenshot, prove the capture shows what is really on screen.
25	  `PrintWindow` lies about GL and modals; `CopyFromScreen` of the window rect does not.
26	- Drive the page's own controls over the WebView2 DevTools protocol when the OS refuses
27	  synthetic input: launch with `REDACTED`,
28	  then `Runtime.evaluate` a real `element.click()` on the target. See
29	  [[windows-ui-testing-without-a-desktop]]. That click goes through the real handler and

11	On 2026-10-14, after a long run of experiment reports on the project assistant's prompt, Kenneth said: "You have to restate everything in plain English, it's very difficult to read your text."
12	
13	The reports he was reacting to were packed with tool names, arm names, "3 of 3" counts, tables and compressed bullet labels.
14	
15	**Why:** he reads these to decide what to do next, often quickly, and he judges results by whether the explanation makes sense in the real world ("the rubber has to meet the road"), not by the numbers from a small test set. He said the same day that with small samples "we cannot just look at the numbers... we need to use common sense to see if the attribution makes sense."
16	
17	**How to apply:** (my interpretation) write to him in ordinary sentences. Say what happened and why it makes sense, as you would to someone who was not watching. Keep code identifiers, arm names and counts to the few that carry the point, and explain a term the first time it appears. Lead with the answer. Prefer a short explanation of cause over a table of outcomes. When passing work to sub-agents, tell them the same: judge by whether the cause is believable, and check results against how the product is really used. See [[fix-without-breaking-other-scenarios]].

3	description: "git commit hangs in Entire's prepare-commit-msg on Windows because Entire opens CONIN$ for a [Y/n] link prompt; GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 makes it non-interactive"
4	metadata:
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project

9	---
10	
11	Root cause (diagnosed 2026-09-25, Entire CLI 0.11.0): when the committing session has file changes to link,
12	`entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg <file> message` shows "Link this commit to session context? [Y/n]" and reads the
13	answer from `CONIN$`, not stdin. The agent's Git Bash has a hidden console, so the open succeeds and the read blocks forever.
14	`</dev/null` does not help. Commits with nothing to link skip the prompt, which is why it looked intermittent.
15	The log is buffered, so `.entire/logs/entire.log` shows nothing until the process exits.
16	Evidence: handle dump of the hung process showed a `\Device\ConDrv` handle with a blocked synchronous read.
17	Entire's own Pi integration prefixes agent bash commands with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` for this exact reason.
18	With `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` the same hook finished in ~0.3s and added the trailer, 3 of 3 runs; without it, 3 of 3 hung.
19	
20	**Why:** It looks like a slow checkpoint condense, so it is easy to wait a long time for nothing.
21	A separate, real slowdown also exists: an `msbuild -m` build pins all 16 cores (processor queue ~64) and every
22	`entire` launch then takes 5-20s. That is slow, not hung; don't confuse the two.
23	
24	**How to apply:** Fixed 2026-09-25: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` is set as a user env var (HKCU\Environment), so Claude and Codex
25	shells inherit it after the app restarts (verified in Claude: 3/3 hook runs 0.3s with trailer). If a commit hangs again, first check
26	`echo $GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` in the agent shell. Restarting the Claude app: the tray has no Quit, so end all `claude` processes
27	from a helper launched via WMI (outside Claude's tree) and relaunch with `explorer.exe shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude`.
28	If one hangs anyway, kill only that commit's `entire` PID; never `--no-verify`. See [[windows-build-machine]].
29	
30	2026-09-27: with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` already set, a `git merge --no-ff` (merge commit) in a worktree still ran past a
31	120 s `timeout` -- but the merge commit was already written correctly and nothing was left running. After a timeout, check
32	`git log -1` and the parents before retrying; a retry would make a second commit. A plain `git commit` minutes earlier took ~seconds.

Worked on 2026-10-02 for the left pane (`shell_integration_harness --manual-left-pane`). Four traps, each of which first looked like a defect in the app:
12	
13	- **Arrow keys need `KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY` (flag 1).** Without it `keybd_event(VK_DOWN)` arrives as `WXK_NUMPAD_DOWN` (379), not `WXK_DOWN` (317), so a handler testing only `WXK_DOWN` looks dead. (Real numpad arrows send the same code, so handlers should accept both.)
14	- **The GL canvas takes keyboard focus when the pointer enters it.** Parking the cursor over the canvas between a click and a key press moves focus off the control under test. Park it inside the surface being tested.
15	- **Coordinates are virtualized, the screen copy is not.** PowerShell is DPI-unaware: `GetWindowRect`/`SetCursorPos` use logical units (screen reads 1728x1084 at 200%), while `CopyFromScreen` wants real pixels. Multiply by `GetDeviceCaps(DESKTOPHORZRES=118) / GetDeviceCaps(HORZRES=8)`.
16	- **Tab is not available for focus traversal**: OrcaSlicer binds it to switching Prepare/Preview, and `wxWindow::Navigate()` is a no-op in this wx build (`wxHAS_NATIVE_TAB_TRAVERSAL`). Fork surfaces must move focus themselves (the left pane does it in a `wxEVT_CHAR_HOOK` handler).
17	
18	**Why:** each cost a rebuild-and-retry loop before the cause turned out to be the instrument, not the code. Same lesson as [[verify-the-basic-path-in-the-app]].
19	
20	**How to apply:** start from a scratch `ui.ps1` with Click-At / Press-Key / Capture helpers built on the rules above; when a key "does nothing", log the key code in the handler before changing the handler.
21	
22	Related harness facts from the same session:
23	- `workspace_adapter_integration_harness.exe` gets no runtime DLLs copied beside it; run it with `C:\b\<tree>\tests\shell\Release` on `PATH` or it exits `0xC0000135`.
24	- In the default shell-harness mode, `failed_autosave_is_visible`, `failed_autosave_has_plain_status_text`, `failed_autosave_blocks_project_release` and `earlier_model_version_available` fail on Windows on an unmodified build too: the test makes a directory read-only with POSIX permissions, which Windows ignores. Since the Check Print crash was fixed (2026-10-14, `20de313d92`) the default mode runs to the end on this box: 552 pass, 6 fail. The other two failures, `agent_panel_columns_tile_the_client_shrinking_to_1000_dip` and `growing_to_1400_dip`, also fail with the fix switched off, with identical geometry, so they predate it. The filament-menu keyboard checks (`down_selects_the_first_filament` etc.) failed in 1 of 4 runs of the same binary, and that run then stalled on an open setup guide. Cause found 2026-10-28: the real mouse pointer resting where the filament menu opens (e.g. 645,513 at 1920x1080) hovers a row, which steals the keyboard selection; 6 checks fail, `one_note_per_menu_visit_that_changed_a_filament` included. name: native-ui-synthetic-input-and-capture
description: "Driving JusPrin's native (wx) UI on the Windows box with real pointer and key input from PowerShell, and capturing it — the four traps that each looked like an app bug"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 5f4606f5-f6a6-45fd-a91f-ea049831eb87
  modified: 2026-10-28T12:17:55.883Z
---

With the RDP session **connected** (see [[windows-ui-testing-without-a-desktop]] for the disconnected case), native wx surfaces can be driven from PowerShell with `SetCursorPos` + `mouse_event` + `keybd_event` and captured with `Graphics.CopyFromScreen`. Worked on 2026-10-02 for the left pane (`shell_integration_harness --manual-left-pane`). Four traps, each of which first looked like a defect in the app:

- **Arrow keys need `KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY` (flag 1).** Without it `keybd_event(VK_DOWN)` arrives as `WXK_NUMPAD_DOWN` (379), not `WXK_DOWN` (317), so a handler testing only `WXK_DOWN` looks dead. (Real numpad arrows send the same code, so handlers should accept both.)
- **The GL canvas takes keyboard focus when the pointer enters it.** Parking the cursor over the canvas between a click and a key press moves focus off the control under test. Park it inside the surface being tested.
- **Coordinates are virtualized, the screen copy is not.** PowerShell is DPI-unaware: `GetWindowRect`/`SetCursorPos` use logical units (screen reads 1728x1084 at 200%), while `CopyFromScreen` wants real pixels. Multiply by `GetDeviceCaps(DESKTOPHORZRES=118) / GetDeviceCaps(HORZRES=8)`.
- **Tab is not available for focus traversal**: OrcaSlicer binds it to switching Prepare/Preview, and `wxWindow::Navigate()` is a no-op in this wx build (`wxHAS_NATIVE_TAB_TRAVERSAL`). Fork surfaces must move focus themselves (the left pane does it in a `wxEVT_CHAR_HOOK` handler).

**Why:** each cost a rebuild-and-retry loop before the cause turned out to be the instrument, not the code. Same lesson as [[verify-the-basic-path-in-the-app]].

**How to apply:** start from a scratch `ui.ps1` with Click-At / Press-Key / Capture helpers built on the rules above; when a key "does nothing", log the key code in the handler before changing the handler.

Related harness facts from the same session:
- `workspace_adapter_integration_harness.exe` gets no runtime DLLs copied beside it; run it with `C:\b\<tree>\tests\shell\Release` on `PATH` or it exits `0xC0000135`.
- In the default shell-harness mode, `failed_autosave_is_visible`, `failed_autosave_has_plain_status_text`, `failed_autosave_blocks_project_release` and `earlier_model_version_available` fail on Windows on an unmodified build too: the test makes a directory read-only with POSIX permissions, which Windows ignores. Since the Check Print crash was fixed (2026-10-14, `20de313d92`) the default mode runs to the end on this box: 552 pass, 6 fail. The other two failures, `agent_panel_columns_tile_the_client_shrinking_to_1000_dip` and `growing_to_1400_dip`, also fail with the fix switched off, with identical geometry, so they predate it. The filament-menu keyboard checks (`down_selects_the_first_filament` etc.) failed in 1 of 4 runs of the same binary, and that run then stalled on an open setup guide. Cause found 2026-10-28: the real mouse pointer resting where the filament menu opens (e.g. 645,513 at 1920x1080) hovers a row, which steals the keyboard selection; 6 checks fail, `one_note_per_menu_visit_that_changed_a_filament` included. Park the pointer off the window (`[System.Windows.Forms.Cursor]::Position`) before a default run. See [[windows-build-machine]].
- A baseline for "is this failure mine": copy `C:\src\JusPrin\build\tests\shell\Release\*` to a scratch dir and run that exe (copying avoids locking the shared build's exe).

name: jusprin-release-publishing
description: "How JusPrin 2.x releases are built and published (jusprin_release.yml, jusprin/vX.Y.Z tags, inherited OrcaSlicer tags, Windows-only test failures)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory

---

On jusprin-newui since 2026-10-23 (13c06c3ff3): `.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml` builds Win x64 / macOS universal / Linux x64 into a DRAFT release; Kenneth publishes by hand. Version comes only from `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`; notes from `Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`. Started by Run workflow (needs the file on the default branch `main`, the only way to tick macOS signing) or by pushing a `jusprin-release/*` branch (always unsigned).

**Why:** the repo still carries OrcaSlicer's own tags v2.0.0..v2.3.1; a draft published on an existing tag lands on that tag's commit. So JusPrin tags are `jusprin/vX.Y.Z` and `Packaging/release.mjs` refuses existing tags.

**How to apply:**
- Drafts are invisible to unauthenticated API calls; the git credential (`git credential fill`) has repo scope and works for the releases API. Never print it.
- On this Windows box, pre-existing failures (also on jusprin-newui without changes): ctest #91 PlaceholderParser coFloatsOrPercents segfault, agent_bridge `pick_attachment` previewText (CRLF), AgentUI vitest projectInstructions/skills (CRLF).
- Profile updates are off by policy (`sync_system_preset=false` in attach_shell); see [[jusprin-state-json-unshipped]] for no-migration context.
- Local Windows packaging check without NSIS (2026-10-25): put a makensis stand-in first on PATH (source `C:\b\evi-stub\makensis.c`: answers `/VERSION`, logs its args, builds nothing) and run `windows_package.ps1`. cpack then stages the files and writes `_CPack_Packages\win64\NSIS\project.nsi`, and fails only at "Problem copying the package"; `-SkipInstaller` builds the portable zip. The exe's Details come from `OrcaSlicer.rc.in` filled by `Packaging/identity.cmake`; `windows_package.ps1` refuses an exe that doesn't say JusPrin / Obico / the release version.

=== b08a307459 2026-10-30 04:55:02 -0700
Send every Agent chat from an append-only record, so provider caches hit

Each request a chat sends is now the record of everything it sent
before, byte for byte, plus what this turn adds. Before, the host
rebuilt the history on every request from the chat's messages, and
seven things changed earlier bytes between requests: a reminder added
at the front, a 64 KiB rolling trim, a 16 KiB cut of old tool results,
skills dropped after their turn, app notes rewritten in place, workspace
and picture stripping, and an unstable tool list. Each one invalidated
the provider's prompt cache from that byte on.

What changed in the Agent:
- ProjectStateDocument keeps a per-chat ChatRecord of the items sent,
  in the wire format they were sent in; pictures are kept beside it
  under chats/<conversation>/ and read back as sent. Items join the
  record only once the provider has accepted the request, so a refused
  request leaves no trace.
- ProviderAgent renders that record on every request and appends the
  turn's own items. A chat talks in one wire format; picking a model of
  another format fails the turn with chat_format_fixed.
- Fired skills and app notes go as operator-role messages (an in-array
  system message on Anthropic, a developer item on Responses) and stay
  in the record. On a direct Anthropic connection a skill is scoped to
  its own request with clear_at; through the gateway and on Responses it
  stays in place.
- Responses requests carry a per-chat prompt_cache_key; object_import is
  offered on every turn so the tool list never changes; the file-load
  reminder, the rolling trim and the result cut are gone.
- A chat-title request keeps nothing in the record.
- A tool call's outcome is announced once, after the save that follows
  it, and the MCP bridge builds with the project's Asio setting so its
  tests no longer hang.

Tests: a [history-prefix] guard checks on both codecs that every request
of a turn opens with the whole previous request. The shell harness logs
every request body as posted (--request-log) and runs a three-chat live
journey on either provider; prefix_check.py reports the first differing
byte between consecutive bodies. The prompt suite is re-recorded on the
record, with its "skill sent once" checks restated as "appended once,
then replayed", and assertions across four test layers now read tool
lists, model ids and profile values from the app instead of copies.

Measured on the same three chats on gpt-5.4-mini: 82.8% of input
tokens served from cache (62.6% before), 19 of 19 consecutive request
pairs pure appends (9 of 16 before), the second request of each chat
cached (0 before). A two-turn chat confirmed Responses accepts replayed
reasoning items with encrypted_content under store:false.

The live prompt suite ran on this change (DeepSeek V4 Flash, three runs
a case, the pinned OpenAI judge): 58 of 66 runs passed over the 22
measurable cases against the previous baseline's 53, no wrong answer,
two host timeouts. Kenneth confirmed that run as the suite's baseline on
2026-10-30; baseline.json and the README's current-baseline section
carry it. file-note-not-instructions moves to noBaseline: its second
request now carries the plate picture, which the pinned DeepSeek hosts
refuse, so it is unmeasurable there like the three picture cases.

=== 30ae01eae0 2026-10-29 15:02:42 -0700
Name each chat to JusPrin's gateway, so it can keep the chat whole

The gateway now keeps each chat's newest request and reply for future
fine-tuning (tsd-enterprise 906752ee3e). Without a chat name it can only
keep each turn separately.

Every reply request to the gateway now carries X-JusPrin-Chat: the first 32
hex digits of SHA-256 over the chat's key, "<projectId>/<conversationId>".
It is the same on every request of a chat and differs between chats. The
project id is random, and a project copy imported on the same machine
already gets a new one (fork_identity), so a copy's chats get new names
without storing anything new in the project. Titles carry no chat key and
so no header. Other providers get nothing.

The key travels as AgentRequest::chat_key, set by
AgentHost::make_agent_request, and TurnTranscript::chat_key. Those lines
are a08d17471f's on claude/chat-history-cache byte for byte, without its
use as OpenAI's prompt_cache_key, so merging that branch later applies
cleanly.

=== 953eddb355 2026-10-29 00:51:45 +0000
Show the first-run screen when no projects folder exists yet

The projects folder is made by the first saved version, so a new data
folder has none. project_folders() tested for it with
is_directory(root, error) and returned an empty list only when that
left the error clear. libc++ (macOS) and MSVC (Windows) both report a
missing path as an error there, so the listing went on, failed, and
returned nothing: Home said "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin
will keep trying." and logged "Local projects could not be listed"
once a second, instead of showing "Drop a model or project to start".

exists(root, error) clears the error for a missing path, as the
standard requires, and keeps every other error (permission denied, I/O
failure), which still reaches the listing and is still logged and
reported. A file where the folder belongs, which is_directory() also
let through as no projects, now fails the listing and is reported.
Both callers, projects() and projects_for_source(), go through this.

- jusprin_tests [home]: 42 test cases pass.
- Real app on an empty --datadir: before, the error screen and the

=== 516d057f1d 2026-10-28 16:14:05 -0700
Accept a hidden preset by name when the project uses it

A 3MF can select a system preset for a printer model the person never
enabled, so OrcaSlicer marks it hidden (is_visible false). JusPrin
refused such a preset by name wherever it checked is_visible, even
while the project was using it. In the 2026-10-28 walkthrough the
selected "Bambu PLA Basic @BBL A1M" made settings_get fail with
unknown_preset, and the error suggested the same name it rejected.

The flag cannot answer "in use" by itself. OrcaSlicer's preset combo
box marks a selected hidden preset visible while it draws, but only
the stored preset: find_preset returns the edited copy for the
selected preset, and that copy keeps the flag it had when selected.

Printers::preset_by_name (new, header-only) accepts a preset that is
visible, selected in its collection, or in one of the project's
filament slots. Every lookup that refused hidden presets now uses it:
- the settings tools' target.preset (scope_preset)
- printer_setup and its preview: printer, process and filament names
- the header's Filament settings... and Printer settings... openers,
  which showed "The ... preset was not found"
- the printer chat's stock-profile lookup (stock_printer)
Hidden presets the project does not use are still refused. Pick
lists (presets_list, the filament chip's INSTALLED rows) keep
filtering on is_visible, which is what the flag is for.

=== ebbb2f8894 2026-10-28 18:54:15 +0000
Print history: record every G-code that leaves a project, show it, print it again

One record per G-code that left a project replaces the Sent events and
physical prints, which nothing outside tests ever wrote. It is shown on one
Print history screen, and any recorded G-code can be printed again from the
file the project kept. Nothing records, badges or draws a failure: a
printer reports a person's stop and a failed print the same way, so a print
that ended early simply never finishes. Slicing writes nothing.

The record (Agent/ManufacturingHistory, Agent/ProjectStateDocument)
- Keyed by the SHA-256 of the plate's sliced G-code, so the same slice
  exported and sent is one record. It holds where the G-code went (exports
  with the exported file's own hash; sends with the printer's name, whether
  the send started the print, when the transport confirmed it, and for a
  Bambu send the hash of the package it uploaded) and the prints the
  printer reported: started, finished. It also holds the slice's estimates
  and layer count, the presets, and the chat item it followed.
- A copy of each G-code that leaves is kept at <project>/gcode/<hash>.gcode,
  the newest 20 per project. A Bambu print also keeps the .gcode.3mf it
  uploaded, byte for byte (and for a cloud printer the config 3MF it also
  sent), pruned with its G-code.
- A document holding the old "sent" and "physicalPrints" arrays loads and
  drops them (no shipped build wrote them).

Writers (Shell/GcodeHistoryRecorder)
- Exports (OrcaSlicer's own and the export_file tool's) through the new
  EVT_OUTPUT_EXPORTED; Bambu prints and uploads through the jobs' finished
  events while their dialog is showing; print-host uploads through the
  queue's new enqueue observer and the queue dialog's progress at 100.
- Bambu printers are polled every two seconds whatever is on screen;
  Agent/PrintOutcomeTracker decides which report belongs to which send, and
  a finish of a project that is not open is written into its saved
  document. Print hosts record sends only.

Print history (HomeUI, Home/PrintHistory, Home/OrcaHomeBackend)
- A second screen of the Home page: one entry per G-code, grouped by day,
  with a row per destination (an export: matches, changed outside JusPrin,
  not found; a send: delivery and whether it started) and per print
  (Printing with its progress, Finished; a stopped one shows only when it
  started). Project and printer are removable filter chips over one list,
  with a search box. Its bar is Back and the title: Preferences is reached
  from the title bar's menu and Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on macOS).
- Ways in: a link in the gallery header, a line on each project card and
  printer card, one row on the project pane's Project tab (replacing its
  old Print history view), and a "history" link on each chat marker. Back
  returns to where it was opened from.
- Open in chat opens the project and scrolls its chat to the marker
  (reveal_item). Export... writes the kept copy and records it; Export again
  on a changed file writes a new file beside it, never over it.
- The chat shows one marker line where a G-code left, in place of the
  retired print card. The model reads the last ten records as printHistory.

Print again, and print_dialog_open
- Sends the kept file, never a fresh slice, always through OrcaSlicer's own
  send dialog; the person presses Send there and nothing in it is set.
- Bambu: the kept package goes to Select Machine the way the printer's file
  browser opens a file (Plater::update_print_required_data,
  EVT_PRINT_FROM_SDCARD_VIEW), with the dialog's new-print flag set so the
  job uploads the local file as a new print. Printing from the printer's
  storage is not used: the file name there is reused for every send of a
  project, so it cannot say which version would print.
- Print hosts with OrcaSlicer's standard upload dialog get a temporary copy
  of the kept G-code (the queue deletes what it uploads). ElegooLink,
  Creality Print, Flashforge's local API and use_3mf hosts are not offered
  Print again; PrusaConnect's readiness question is not asked.
- Offered only when the kept file is there and still hashes as kept;
  otherwise the entry says why and to slice again (a kept file changed on
  disk is logged as an error and never sent).
- print_dialog_open (in-app and MCP) opens the dialog for a plate's slice,
  refused with needs_step naming slice_start when it has none, or with
  gcode for a recorded G-code.

rewritten). The fork owns these seams; the policy is in fork files.
- Plater.hpp/.cpp: EVT_OUTPUT_EXPORTED, declared and defined, sent

=== 2d3fc8157a 2026-10-28 12:09:50 -0700
Wait out web view setup before leaving the JusPrin view

The default shell harness run failed return_keeps_the_project_chat and
then stopped without a result line: it segfaulted on the second switch
to classic view.

The crash: a shell that has just come back from classic view creates
new web views, and on macOS each one installs its "wx" script message
handler from a CallAfter, waiting for WebKit's answer in a nested event
loop with is_adding_script_handler() set. A switch to classic view
chosen right then ran inside that wait, uninstalled the shell, and
freed the web views under the install. detach_shell() now retries on a
50 ms timer while an install is in progress, the same wait
GUI_App::run_wizard and PrinterPanel make. The harness's own exit
closed the frame inside the same wait right after the banner return,
so its finish() waits too.

The lost draft was in the harness. In the default run the step before
replaces the project, and ProjectPersistence settles that replacement
on the shell's pacing timer or the next workspace event. Until then the
document is still the previous project's, so the fixture recorded the
old project id and wrote the draft into the old document, which the
replacement then discarded. The fixture now settles the pending
boundary first with the persistence's public
resolve_pending_boundary().

Only fork-owned files change. Verified on macOS: the default run,
--classic-switch and --stock each print HARNESS RESULT PASS failures=0
and exit 0.

checkpoint file is named ".3mf", as Orca's own crash backup is.

flag, false by default. When set, load_external_preset first tries the
saved name, and falls back to Orca's usual naming if another preset already
has it.

=== 660f845e00 2026-10-26 16:19:40 -0700
Stop macOS popups from touching a destroyed hovered row

On macOS, OrcaSlicer's PopupWindow remembers the child under the pointer
in a raw pointer so it can send that child a leave event on the next
mouse move. JusPrin's header menus destroy and rebuild every row when the
menu changes step (for example Printer > Plate), so the next mouse move
could send the event to freed memory and crash the app with
EXC_BAD_ACCESS in PopupWindow::OnMouseEvent2. It crashed only sometimes,
because a rebuild usually puts a new row at the freed address.

The pointer is now a wxWeakRef, which becomes null when its target is
destroyed, and the leave event is skipped when the row is gone.

The shell harness gains a check that hovers a menu separator, destroys
it, and moves the pointer again. Run with MallocScribble=1 so a stale
pointer crashes reliably: before this change the harness exited with
SIGSEGV at that step; after it, all 565 default checks and all 24
--stock checks pass.

Upstream-owned file: four lines in PopupWindow.cpp/.hpp changed in
place (field type, a null check around the leave event, .get() before
two casts) plus one include; no logic moved or deleted. Both files merge
cleanly onto upstream/main ee6d195b0e from fork base 3ffb9585d2, and
upstream has not changed this macOS code.

the --auto-slice mode.

1225	Stop macOS popups from touching a destroyed hovered row
1226	
1227	On macOS, OrcaSlicer's PopupWindow remembers the child under the pointer
1228	in a raw pointer so it can send that child a leave event on the next
1229	mouse move. JusPrin's header menus destroy and rebuild every row when the
1230	menu changes step (for example Printer > Plate), so the next mouse move
1231	could send the event to freed memory and crash the app with
1232	EXC_BAD_ACCESS in PopupWindow::OnMouseEvent2. It crashed only sometimes,
1233	because a rebuild usually puts a new row at the freed address.
1234	
1235	The pointer is now a wxWeakRef, which becomes null when its target is
1236	destroyed, and the leave event is skipped when the row is gone.

1238	The shell harness gains a check that hovers a menu separator, destroys
1239	it, and moves the pointer again. Run with MallocScribble=1 so a stale
1240	pointer crashes reliably: before this change the harness exited with
1241	SIGSEGV at that step; after it, all 565 default checks and all 24
1242	--stock checks pass.

The project prompt tests now run only the new version and compare it with
a baseline kept in the repository, and setup_record loses its requirement
fields. The run without the fields is the new DeepSeek baseline.

A stored baseline

A prompt change was judged by running the old and new prompt side by side.
Now the runner runs only the checkout and ends by printing every case beside
a stored baseline: baseline.json for DeepSeek V4 Flash on the pinned hosts
with the OpenAI judge, baseline-claude-cli.json for the subscription. Each
holds the backend, model, hosts, judge, date and commit it was recorded at,
the SHA-256 of its prompt, tool list and recording, and per case the runs,
passes, fails and unobserved runs; noBaseline names the cases it has no
counts for and why.

The comparison marks only large moves: a case's share of passing runs moving
by 60% of its runs or more, which at three runs is 3 of 3 against 1 or 0 of
3. It flags marks that may be host noise (a drop made of unobserved runs or
request errors, three or more cases dropping at once), says when the tool
list or recording differ from the baseline's, and refuses to compare a run
on another model, hosts or judge. The exit code is 1 when a case is marked
worse; --must-pass keeps the old rule. --results saves a run in the
baseline's form, --compare compares a saved run without sending anything,
and --record-baseline makes a full run (or a saved one) the new baseline.
The README says when to re-record: after Kenneth accepts a deliberate
change, or when the model, hosts or judge change. test_steps.py checks the
marking, the recording and that both files name exactly the current cases.

Removing setup_record's fields

setup_record took, beside the purpose and the plan, a list of fields:
requirement names the model chose, each with a value, a question or an
assumed flag. They are removed end to end, because:

  2026-10-07) nothing confirms them, yet the coordinator stored each one as
  user_confirmed unless the model said it assumed it.
- They went back to the model on every turn in the <workspace> block
  (ProviderAgent's intent block), which the prompt calls the app's own data,
  so the model's guesses returned to it as the person's confirmed facts.
- Their only other reader was slice_report's intent section
  (Agent/IntentChecks.hpp): regex parsing that read "holds a 5 kg backpack"
  as a weight limit and metres as minutes, summed ranges, and worked only in
  English.
- The page never showed them, and no prompt case checked them.

- ToolRegistry: setup_record has no fields argument (a call with one is
  refused) and its result no intent section; its description no longer
  mentions them. workspace_inspect and slice_report lose their intent
  sections. purposeChange is first, changed or unchanged: with the fields
  gone the purpose is the setup title alone, so a different purpose is a
  changed purpose and fires the setup skill (it used to be "title_only",
  which fired nothing).

  the intent fields, IntentField and Provenance. A purpose is recorded when
  the chat has a setup title. A chat's stored printIntent is no longer read

  messages in their source English, and a Windows fault in the file-load
  report's fitsSelectedBed (false for a 20 mm cube on the X1 Carbon); the

conversation (a time limit, a dimension) shaping the setup many turns later.

The new DeepSeek baseline

Kenneth confirmed the run of 2026-10-25 without the fields as the new
baseline: all 26 cases three times, 56 passed, 5 failed and 8 unobserved in
the 23 measured (the three picture cases get HTTP 404 from the hosts).

current-baseline section describes the run, and the 2026-10-19 one moves to
the baseline history.

cube on the X1 Carbon included. loaded_object_facts looped over
convex_hull_2d().points, a member Polygon inherits from MultiPoint, of a
temporary. MSVC destroys such a temporary before the loop runs, so the
footprint was empty and fits_bed refused it; Clang extends the temporary,

user_import_tiny_object_fits_and_is_on_the_bed, which failed on Windows for

# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)

Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.

The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
`orca`.

**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.

Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. JusPrin turns `single_instance` on at every start; its instance lock
lives in the data directory, so a scratch `--datadir` runs as its own instance
beside another JusPrin. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

For an MCP client, the shell harness does all of this in its own datadir:
`shell_integration_harness --manual-mcp <dir> --fake-printer` saves a

# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)

Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.

The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
`orca`.

**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.

Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. JusPrin turns `single_instance` on at every start; its instance lock
lives in the data directory, so a scratch `--datadir` runs as its own instance
beside another JusPrin. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Test Suite Organization

### libslic3r Tests
Core slicing engine tests covering:
- **Geometry operations**: Points, polygons, lines, Voronoi diagrams
- **File formats**: STL, 3MF, AMF parsing and validation
- **Algorithms**: Clipper operations, mesh boolean operations, optimization
- **Configuration**: Print settings validation and parsing
- **Utilities**: String processing, time utilities, data structures

### fff_print Tests
Fused Filament Fabrication specific tests:
- **G-code generation**: Writer functionality, cooling, lift/unlift
- **Slicing algorithms**: Layer generation, infill patterns
- **Print mechanics**: Flow calculations, extrusion, support material
- **Model processing**: Print objects, skirt/brim generation

### sla_print Tests
Stereolithography specific tests:
- **SLA print processing**: Layer curing, support generation
- **Raycast operations**: Light path calculations
- **Test utilities**: SLA-specific helper functions

## Writing New Tests - Best Practices

### File Organization
1. **Naming Convention**: `test_<feature>.cpp` (e.g., `test_geometry.cpp`)
2. **Header Structure**: Include `<catch2/catch_all.hpp>` first, then relevant headers
3. **Namespace Usage**: Use `using namespace Slic3r;` for convenience
4. **File Placement**: Add to appropriate test directory and update CMakeLists.txt

### Test Naming and Structure
```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>
#include "libslic3r/Point.hpp"

using namespace Slic3r;

TEST_CASE("Feature description", "[category_tag]") {
    // Test implementation
}
```

### Tagging System
Use descriptive tags for test categorization:
- `[Geometry]` - Geometric operations and calculations
- `[GCodeWriter]` - G-code generation functionality  
- `[Config]` - Configuration and settings tests
- `[FileFormat]` - File I/O operations (STL, 3MF, etc.)
- `[Algorithm]` - Core algorithms and processing
- `[Performance]` - Performance benchmarks (if applicable)

## Catch2 Features Guide

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

file.content:
---
name: crash-stacks-without-a-debugger
description: "Get a symbolized call stack for a native crash on the Windows box in minutes: C:\\b\\minidbg (Win32 debug API) plus a build tree compiled with /Z7 and linked /DEBUG; traps that cost a full rebuild"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: c04fbdd1-d707-42dc-922c-7911bb1d35e0
  modified: 2026-10-14T17:09:52.100Z
---

`C:\b\minidbg\minidbg.exe <exe> [args]` (source `minidbg.cpp` beside it, built with `cl /std:c++17 /EHsc /DUNICODE`) runs a program under the Win32 debug API and prints a symbolized stack, with file:line where a PDB exists, for every access violation, heap corruption, stack-buffer overrun and second-chance exception. No WinDbg download needed. Set `_NO_DEBUG_HEAP=1`. `run-harness-example.ps1` there shows the env setup for the shell harness. Used 2026-10-14 to find the Check Print crash: the stack led straight to `GCodeViewer::init` → `strlen(glGetString(GL_VERSION))` with no current GL context.

For line numbers you need a tree with debug info. Configure with
`"-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE=/MD /O2 /Ob2 /DNDEBUG /Z7"`, the same for C, and `"-DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_RELEASE=/DEBUG:FULL /OPT:REF /OPT:ICF"` (example: `C:\b\ckp-build.cmd`). **Keep `/MD`.** Overriding the flags without it compiles everything `/MT`, and the link fails only at the very end with `LNK2038 RuntimeLibrary mismatch` against opencv/libcurl, after a 40-minute build. `SLIC3R_MSVC_PDB` is declared in CMakeLists.txt but nothing reads it.

Quick triage without any of this: the event-log fault offset in a system DLL maps to a function via `dumpbin /exports <dll>` (the nearest export at or below the offset). ucrtbase `0x2a341` is `strlen+0x31`, meaning a null or bad `char*`.

Run harnesses with `Start-Process -RedirectStandardError` rather than PowerShell `2>`. A PowerShell native-command redirect writes the file only when the process exits, so a hung run shows a 0-byte log. Visible windows of a stuck process can be listed with `C:\b\ckp-windows.ps1 -ProcessId <pid>` (a `#32770` titled 引导_P21 is OrcaSlicer's setup guide left open).

Windows GL fact found the same day: `wxGLCanvas::Create` on MSW always ends with `wglMakeCurrent(nullptr, nullptr)`. Creating any GL canvas leaves no context current, so GL work right after constructing a canvas needs an explicit make-current first.
